==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*kewh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|coward}}, from {{der|en|fro|coart}}, {{m|fro|cuard}} ( > {{cog|fr|couard}}), from {{m|fro|coue|t=tail}}, ''coe'' + {{m|fro|-ard|pos=pejorative agent noun suffix}}; {{m|fro|coue}}, ''coe'' is in turn from {{der|en|la|cauda}}. The reference seems to be to an animal "[[turning tail]]", or having its tail between its legs, especially a dog. Compare the expression {{m|en|tail between one's legs}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|earg}} (surviving in northern dialect {{noncog|en|argh}}). Unrelated to {{m|en|cower}}, which is of Germanic origin. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|kou'əd|a=UK}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈkaʊəd/}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-coward.wav|a=Southern England}} *
